summary: Tenant sessions routed to cost-fallback variant despite active version pin after prewarm reconciliation
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10T08:20 UTC a single enterprise tenant (FinOrbit) observed intermittent requests returning responses from the cost-optimized fallback variant while their route is explicitly pinned to finorbit/gpt-fin-4.0-hrq. Impact: customer saw incorrect model behavior and a 2x spike in token billing (fallback variant has higher per-token cost due to routing mis-classification). Environment: production cluster in us-east-1, Dedicated pool assigned to FinOrbit with explicit version pin configured in Console. Observable window: ~08:20–09:40 UTC on 2026-03-10.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant configured with explicit model_version pin to finorbit/gpt-fin-4.0-hrq via Console (tenant id: finorbit-772).
2) Trigger steady stream of chat requests (50 RPS) and verify pinned model in request headers (X-Model-Pin).
3) Observe routing decisions in /v1/routing/decide logs during prewarm/reconciliation window (scheduled prewarm job ran at 08:15 UTC).
4) Reproduce by running synthetic traffic while toggling prewarm reconciliation from console (dev-only) — NOTE: reproduction requires dedicated pool and scheduled prewarm event.
logs: 2026-03-10T08:15:03.118Z orchestrator:prewarm INFO starting prewarm reconcile shard=12
2026-03-10T08:15:03.221Z metrics-agg WARN last_heartbeat_age=18s for shard=12; aggregator TTL=15s
2026-03-10T08:20:27.992Z edge-router DEBUG decide-route tenant=finorbit-772 req_id=cb2f4a model_pin=finorbit/gpt-fin-4.0-hrq route_decision=fallback_variant(reason=policy_cost_heuristic)
2026-03-10T08:20:28.007Z billing INFO estimate_cost_diff tenant=finorbit-772 pinned=0.0048$/token fallback=0.0096$/token delta=+100%
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Customer confirm that Console still shows pinned version and there was no manual override. Edge logs show X-Model-Pin present in request and acknowledged by edge-router, yet subsequent routing call to orchestrator returned fallback_variant.

SRE snapshot: orchestrator prewarm reconciliation kicks off and asks metrics-aggregator for a fresh capacity view. Metrics-aggregator returned a stale view because of a brief indexing GC; TTL check in orchestrator treated view as outdated and flipped into conservative routing mode that prefers low-latency fallback variants.

Hypothesis: a TTL mismatch between metrics-aggregator and orchestrator prewarm gating caused the orchestrator to ignore authoritative pin metadata and apply a fallback policy. The check path erroneously set 'stale_capacity_view' which triggers an automated pin eviction in codepath ORCH-RouteGuard.

Reproduced in staging by artificially injecting delay into metrics-aggregator's heartbeat: same behavior — route decision favors fallback_variant and evict_pin log appears within 200ms of prewarm reconcile start.

Edge case: tenant-specific reserved capacity existed and serving nodes were healthy; evict_pin is conservative but unnecessary for dedicated customers. Logic should skip eviction for enterprise-dedicated tenants when a valid pin exists.
resolution: Mitigation performed 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: temporary mitigation applied via Console -> override routing policy for finorbit-772 to 'honor-pin' which prevents ORCH-RouteGuard from evicting pins during reconciliation windows. Customer verified resumed correct model responses and billing delta stopped. Permanent fix: merged PR github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/14286 which adjusts RouteGuard to consult the tenant reservation registry and treat a fresh pin as authoritative despite short TTL misses by metrics-aggregator. Follow-ups: 1) increase metrics-aggregator heartbeat TTL and add circuit breaker to prevent GC-induced staleness, 2) add an alert when RouteGuard performs >5 pin-evictions/min for dedicated tenants, 3) add an e2e canary test simulating aggregator delays to catch regression. Scheduled rollout of fix to prod on 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC with phased wave across us-east-1 orchestrator shards.
